faqs.general.questions.one.title: What is Joint Protocol?
faqs.general.questions.one.content: The Joint protocol is a collection of smart contracts that work together to allow users to trade cryptocurrencies for fiat. The Joint protocol is the decentralized equivalent of P2P exchanges like Localbitcoin and Binance..
faqs.general.questions.two.title: What can I do with Joint Protocol?
faqs.general.questions.two.content: You can use the Joint Protocol to exchange any cryptocurrency for local currencies. For example, you can exchange ETH/USDT/BTC for fiat using any payment method.
faqs.general.questions.three.title: What trading pairs are supported?
faqs.general.questions.three.content: Joint Protocol allows anyone to create a market for any two ERC20 tokens. Furthermore, unlike centralized exchanges, Joint protocol has no trading pair limitation.
faqs.general.questions.four.title: Who are the protocol participants?
faqs.general.questions.four.content: Protocol participants are persons or entities that work together to keep the protocol lively. These are the protocol participants 1. Market Creator - They create markets that can be traded on. 2. Liquidity Provider - Adds and manages liquidity in a market. 3. Liquidity Manager - Optionally granted the power to set or update a liquidity's price. 4. Mediator - Responsible for resolving disputes. 5. Miner - Executes public operations (ex: drafting, un-drafting, vote execution etc.). 6. Interface developer - Provides and manages an interface that allows users quickly access and use the protocol.
faqs.general.questions.five.title: Who is a taker?
faqs.general.questions.five.content: A taker (or swapper) is a person who swaps a quote asset for the base asset of any market.
faqs.general.questions.six.title: What is an Interface?
faqs.general.questions.six.content: An interface is a dApp built on top of the Joint protocol. It can be a web or mobile application. Anyone can build an interface for the Joint protocol with additional features. The beauty of Joint protocol is that all interfaces intrinsically adhere to the protocol's censorship-resistant and non-custodial qualities.
faqs.general.questions.seven.title: Is KYC required?
faqs.general.questions.seven.content: As a collection of smart contracts deployed on the blockchain, the protocol does not require KYC registration. However, interface developers incorporated in regions where KYC is mandatory may require KYC.
faqs.general.questions.eight.title: How are disputes resolved?
faqs.general.questions.eight.content: The Joint protocol comes with a decentralized dispute system that is open, transparent and simple to understand. When a dispute is raised, a minimum of 3 dispute resolvers (a.k.a. Mediators) are randomly drafted to the dispute, where they collect evidence and vote on a verdict. Mediators are paid by the protocol when they vote with the majority and are slashed when they vote with the minority.
faqs.general.questions.nine.title: Can I appeal the outcome of a dispute?
faqs.general.questions.nine.content: Yes! The resolution of a dispute can be appealed within a duration. Therefore, trade participants can perpetually re-appeal a dispute as long the appeal duration has not elapsed. However, to prevent the appeal system from being abused, it will cost a fee to appeal a resolved dispute. In fact, for every re-appeal made, the number of mediators drafted and the fee are doubled.
faqs.general.questions.ten.title: How will Joint protocol be governed?
faqs.general.questions.ten.content: The Joint Team will initially develop the Joint Protocol. When the protocol matures, a co-governance system between the protocol inventors and the community will be set up to manage the protocol. Before maturity, Joint Labs will use snapshot for temperature and consensus checks.
faqs.security.questions.one.title: Is Joint Protocol non-custodian?
faqs.security.questions.one.content: Yes. You will always control your assets in both open and closed markets. No one can prevent you from leaving a market at any time. Your asset leaves your wallet only when you enter a trade, and the smart contract escrow locks your asset until the trade is completed.
faqs.security.questions.two.title: Is Joint Protocol Audited?
faqs.security.questions.two.content: Joint Protocol will be audited before the mainnet launch.
faqs.security.questions.three.title: What happens if a counterparty refuses to release an asset?
faqs.security.questions.three.content: You can start a dispute if you have made the payment requested in the swap order. Joint Protocol’s dispute system brings real humans into a dispute to verify why an asset has not been released or a payment has not been made. The dispute system will release the asset to you if the evidence indicates that you made a payment.
faqs.security.questions.four.title: What happens if a counterparty does not make a payment?
faqs.security.questions.four.content: Suppose a counterparty does not make payment (or mark the swap order as paid). In that case, Joint Protocol will eventually allow the swap order to be cancelled by you or the counterparty after some time elapses. However, you can start a dispute if the counterparty marks the swap order as paid, but you did not receive the payment. Joint Protocol’s dispute system brings real humans into the dispute to verify whether the payment was sent and received. The swap order will be cancelled if payment is not made. However, if it was decided that payment was made, the asset is released to the counterparty.
faqs.security.questions.five.title: Are users on Joint Protocol verified?
faqs.security.questions.five.content: Joint Protocol includes a verification protocol that allows verification service providers to offer Joint Protocol different verification types. Users may use the verification system to get verified for KYC as a token holder, a DAO member, and so on. Market creators and users can filter users based on what verification matters to them. For example, if you wish to swap with KYC-verified users, you can filter markets and liquidity providers by such preference.
faqs.markets.questions.one.title: What is a market?
faqs.markets.questions.one.content: On Joint Protocol, A market is where buyers and sellers of an asset meet to exchange an asset. For example, the Joint protocol market comprises a base and quote asset; Liquidity providers add the base asset while the takers swap the quote asset for the base asset.
faqs.markets.questions.two.title: What are the types of markets?
faqs.markets.questions.two.content: The Joint protocol supports open and permissioned markets. Open markets do not require permission to trade, provide liquidity or mediate. On the other hand, permissioned markets require users to be explicitly permitted to trade, provide liquidity or mediate. Permissioned markets exist to serve private markets with specific admission rules.
faqs.markets.questions.three.title: Can I perform an instant swap between on-chain assets?
faqs.markets.questions.three.content: Yes! Joint Protocol works for on-chain trade pairs like ETH-WBTC etc. Markets that feature only on-chain pairs are called instant markets because the swap will be executed in one transaction.
faqs.markets.questions.four.title: What is a market fee?
faqs.markets.questions.four.content: It is a fee deducted from every trade made in a specific market and paid to the market creator. The market creator sets market fees.
faqs.markets.questions.five.title: Can a market creator set a minimum mediator bond?
faqs.markets.questions.five.content: Yes. Market creators can set how much bond a mediator’s ticket must have before joining the market to provide mediation service. The higher the bond, the more careful and thoughtful a mediator would be in appeals.
faqs.liquidity.questions.one.title: Who is a liquidity provider?
faqs.liquidity.questions.one.content: A liquidity provider is anyone who provides the base asset of a market.
faqs.liquidity.questions.two.title: Who sets the liquidity price?
faqs.liquidity.questions.two.content: Liquidity providers can set the price of their liquidity at all times. They can also delegate the task to a liquidity manager (ex: a price bot).
faqs.liquidity.questions.three.title: Who is a liquidity manager?
faqs.liquidity.questions.three.content: A liquidity manager is another wallet authorized to update the price of liquidity. Users may optionally grant permission to another wallet to help them keep the price of their liquidity close to the market price. Ideally, a price bot should be granted this role.
faqs.liquidity.questions.four.title: Can I add or remove liquidity?
faqs.liquidity.questions.four.content: Yes! Liquidity providers can add or remove liquidity at any time.
faqs.liquidity.questions.five.title: Do liquidity providers earn a fee?
faqs.liquidity.questions.five.content: No. Unlike AMM exchanges, liquidity providers on Joint protocol are more similar to makers on centralized exchanges; they do not earn a fee. They can only set the price of their liquidity. However, at launch, there will be listing and trading rewards that will eventually dry out when the allocation is depleted.
faqs.liquidity.questions.six.title: How many open swap orders can I have?
faqs.liquidity.questions.six.content: The Joint protocol allows a maximum of 5 open swap orders.
faqs.liquidity.questions.seven.title: Can I set the duration I expect to handle payment?
faqs.liquidity.questions.seven.content: Yes. Liquidity providers can set a duration they expect to receive a payment (if they are swapping an on-chain asset) or send payment (if they are swapping fiat or any off-chain asset). After this time elapses, the protocol will enter into a grace period. If the grace period ends without the trade being marked as paid, it will enter the cancellation phase, where the liquidity provider or the taker can cancel the trade.
faqs.liquidity.questions.eight.title: When can I cancel a trade?
faqs.liquidity.questions.eight.content: After the liquidity provider's preferred payment window and the protocol's grace duration elapsed, at that point, any of the participants can cancel the trade.
faqs.liquidity.questions.nine.title: When can I start a dispute?
faqs.liquidity.questions.nine.content: Disputes can be started after the trade has been marked as PAID.
faqs.mediation.questions.one.title: Who is a mediator?
faqs.mediation.questions.one.content: On Joint protocol, a mediator is a real person responsible for deciding the outcome of a dispute. They typically work with other mediators to decide the ruling for a dispute.
faqs.mediation.questions.two.title: How can I become a mediator?
faqs.mediation.questions.two.content: To become a mediator, you must purchase a mediator ticket and stake a minimum amount of P2P tokens to be used as a security bond. The security bond is designed to encourage thoughtful and responsible mediation. But unfortunately, a portion of the mediator's bond is slashed and burned whenever a mediator gets it wrong.
faqs.mediation.questions.three.title: What is the cost of a mediator ticket?
faqs.mediation.questions.three.content: The cost of a mediator ticket is determined by the supply and demand of tickets at a point in time. Joint protocol calculates the prices based on supply and demand. If the demand for tickets is high, the price will rise. When demand is low, the price falls.
faqs.mediation.questions.four.title: What is ticket maturity?
faqs.mediation.questions.four.content: Ticket maturity describes how long a ticket must wait before it is ready to join a market. A newly purchased ticket must wait for time to elapse before it is considered mature. Ticket maturity prevents an attacker from purchasing a ticket and immediately joining a market to influence mediation.
faqs.mediation.questions.five.title: Can a mediator ticket expire?
faqs.mediation.questions.five.content: Yes! Mediator tickets cannot be idle for an extended period or stashed for future use. If a ticket has yet to join a market after purchase, it will expire after some time.The owner can cancel an expired ticket, allowing the security bond to be reclaimed.
faqs.mediation.questions.six.title: Can I delegate my ticket to another wallet?
faqs.mediation.questions.six.content: Yes. A ticket can be delegated to other wallets, allowing those wallets to vote on behalf of the ticket owner. The ticket will still be slashed if the delegates vote wrongly or miss a voting phase.
faqs.mediation.questions.seven.title: Can I resell a mediator ticket?
faqs.mediation.questions.seven.content: No. Ticket owners cannot transfer tickets to another wallet. They can only delegate their ticket to another wallet.
faqs.mediation.questions.eight.title: What does it mean to join a market?
faqs.mediation.questions.eight.content: To join a market means to offer your service as a mediator. Before joining, you will need a mature ticket with a required amount of P2P tokens (security bonds). The market determines the amount of security bond required.
faqs.mediation.questions.nine.title: How many markets can a ticket join?
faqs.mediation.questions.nine.content: A ticket can only join one market at a time. The ticket owner cannot rejoin a market with another ticket.
faqs.mediation.questions.ten.title: Can a ticket leave a market at any time?
faqs.mediation.questions.ten.content: No! Once a ticket joins a market, it must remain in the market for a duration before it can leave the market. This rule exists to limit the ability of bad actors to bribe and collude with mediators to attack a market at a moment's notice.
faqs.mediation.questions.eleven.title: How does drafting work?
faqs.mediation.questions.eleven.content: Miners perform drafting, a category of protocol participants that helps to maintain the protocol's liveliness through the execution of tasks. Miners are responsible for drafting mediators into disputes.
faqs.mediation.questions.twelve.title: What is un-drafting?
faqs.mediation.questions.twelve.content: Un-drafting removes a mediator from a dispute after the dispute has been executed or abandoned. Miners are responsible for un-drafting.
faqs.mediation.questions.thirteen.title: How does voting work?
faqs.mediation.questions.thirteen.conten: When mediator tickets get drafted to a dispute, the dispute will enter into an evidence phase where the mediators will have some time to request and review evidence from the trading participants. After the evidence phase, the vote-committing phase begins. In this phase, mediators must encrypt and cast their votes, requiring a blockchain transaction. After the vote-commit phase, the vote-reveal phase begins. In this phase, mediators must reveal the vote they previously committed; this will also require a transaction.After the vote-reveal phase ends, the appeal phase will begin. In this phase, the outcome of the vote is already known. Therefore, any appeal must be made within this phase, or the ruling will be considered final.  After the appeal phase, the vote is tallied, and the outcome is executed by the smart contract with the help of miners.
faqs.mediation.questions.fourteen.title: What happens if I vote with the minority?
faqs.mediation.questions.fourteen.conten: A fraction of your ticket's security bond will be slashed, and you will be removed from the market.
faqs.mediation.questions.fiveteen.title: What happens if I miss a vote?
faqs.mediation.questions.fiveteen.conten: A fraction of your ticket's security bond will be slashed, and you will be removed from the market.
faqs.mediation.questions.sixteen.title: Do mediators earn a reward?
faqs.mediation.questions.sixteen.content: Yes. Mediators are rewarded for their service to the protocol.
faqs.miners.questions.one.title: Who is a miner?
faqs.miners.questions.one.content: A miner is a user that executes public operations that keep the protocol lively. Public operations are actions that anyone can perform. Miners are responsible for the following: 1. mediators to disputes 2.Un-drafting mediators. 3.Executing dispute ruling. 4.Transferring protocol revenue to staking pools.
faqs.miners.questions.two.title: Is mining incentivized?
faqs.miners.questions.two.content: Yes. Miners are rewarded via inflation; new P2P tokens are minted as a reward for mining.
faqs.miners.questions.three.title: How can I become a miner?
faqs.miners.questions.three.content: There are no special criteria for miners. It is as simple as connecting your wallet and clicking a button to initiate and sign transactions.
